summary.headline: Molbio Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue ₹408 crore with 25% EBITDA margin and PAT ₹52.7 crore; FY27 guidance ~25% top-line growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was ₹408 crore in Q1 FY27, with 164 devices and 62.4 lakh test kits sold. EBITDA was ₹104 crore (25% margin) and PAT ₹52.7 crore (about 13%). Export revenue was about ₹67 crore (16% of revenue), helped by a catch-up of orders deferred from Q4 FY26 due to Gulf disruption. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of roughly 25% and EBITDA margin of 24–25%, while cautioning that quarters are non-linear and OptraScan will not be profitable in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Export ~₹67 crore (16% of revenue), includes catch-up of Q4 FY26 deferrals

financial_highlights.value: Molbio standalone ~₹399 crore; Prognosys ~₹11 crore; OptraScan minimal

financial_highlights.metric: OptraScan loss (Q1 FY27 and comparable 5-month period FY26)

segments.name: Truenat molecular platform (core)
segments.commentary: Kits are about 75% of revenue; installed base ~12,500 machines in 90+ countries, 43 assays across 30 diseases; 40M+ cumulative tests. Gross margin 60–63% across devices and kits per management.

segments.name: Prognosys (70% subsidiary, digital X-ray)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹154 crore and PAT ~₹12 crore; management expects similar ~19% EBITDA margin in FY27. Q1 FY27 revenue ~₹11 crore; US FDA approval for digital imaging and EU MDR for X-ray products.

segments.name: OptraScan (60% subsidiary, digital pathology)
segments.commentary: US FDA clearance received July 2026 for end-to-end workflow incl. software and AI; ~$30 million fresh equity invested. Not expected to be profitable in FY27; meaningful contribution expected FY28–FY29.

segments.name: Bigtec Labs (100% R&D subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Bangalore R&D entity with 150+ scientists and 220+ total staff; intercompany kit sales to Bigtec are eliminated on consolidation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at roughly 25%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 24–25%.
Prognosys expected to deliver ~19% EBITDA margin in FY27, similar to FY26.
OptraScan not expected to be profitable in FY27; meaningful contribution expected in FY28 and FY29.
Device sales expected in the 2,200–2,600 range for the year, in line with historical levels.
HPV-related revenue timing and volumes to be guided next quarter; R&D to stay at 5–6% of revenue.
capex_capacity: IPO proceeds ~₹200 crore: ~₹72 crore for automation and ~₹105 crore for an integrated R&D centre in Bangalore consolidating Bigtec staff.
Current utilisation: ~58% for test kits and ~42% for devices; management says minimal capex can allow doubling of top line from FY26 levels.
Facilities: two kit plants in Goa, device manufacturing in Vizag, a small kit facility in Bangalore, and a Pune site for OptraScan.
Any further manufacturing consolidation in Goa to be funded from internal accruals; no major capex planned beyond what is disclosed.
Certifications: MDSAP; EU IVDR for Truenat CT/NG; EU MDR for X-ray; US FDA for Prognosys imaging and OptraScan.
demand_pricing: TB remains the bulk of the Truenat test mix, mainly public health; management says pricing is similar across diseases in public health.

Government of India HPV validation led by AIIMS; recommended for national rollout; health technology assessment found it cost-effective for women aged 30–45. Volumes not yet quantified; WHO prequalification application in progress.
Two-year TB rate contract with the government signed last month.
India molecular diagnostics share cited at ~90%; ~8,000–9,000 of an estimated 25,000–30,000 TB diagnostic centres are on Truenat.
Pricing is contract-based, not MRP-led; realisation moves driven by device variant mix (Uno/Duo/Quattro), geography and dollar movements.
Export business started around 2023; distributors in 90 countries; ramp expected to take longer, with EU and US entry being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on the HPV tender and test kit off-take?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approvals are in place and a recommendation has been made to roll out the test in the national programme; volumes will be clearer by next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the life cycle of a Truenat device and are consumables exclusive?
qa_highlights.answer: Devices have not needed replacement; early 2017–18 installations are still running. The system is closed, so only Molbio cartridges and chips are used; each test consumes one cartridge or chip.

qa_highlights.question: What R&D and capex are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D at 5–6% of revenue; ₹72 crore automation and ~₹105 crore Bangalore R&D centre are the major capex items; no other major capex planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split and subsidiary profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Molbio standalone ~₹399 crore, Prognosys ~₹11 crore, OptraScan minimal. FY26 Prognosys revenue ₹154 crore, PAT ~₹12 crore; OptraScan loss ~₹9 crore in the period.

qa_highlights.question: Is device volume growing and how will the TB/other-disease mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Device sales expected in the 2,200–2,600 range, in line with history; kit volumes in Q1 were well above Q4 FY26. Non-TB assays such as HPV and hepatitis expected to contribute meaningfully over 2–3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the TB market share sustainable and what is the realisation trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Truenat is the only WHO-endorsed battery-operated point-of-care TB test; remaining centres use microscopy. Pricing is contract-based; realisation moves reflect device mix and FX, with gross margin of 60–63%.

risks_watch: Quarterly lumpiness: management asks investors to track annually; Q1 was helped by export catch-up of Q4 FY26 deferrals linked to the Gulf situation.
OptraScan loss-making in FY27 and ramp dependent on US lab and hospital adoption after July 2026 FDA clearance.
HPV national-programme volumes and timing not yet quantified; next guidance deferred to next quarter.
Inventory days still high at 230 (trailing 12M), though down from 280 in March.
Export ramp slower than expected; past export volumes have been uneven.
Dependence on public-health TB programme for the bulk of domestic revenue under a two-year rate contract.
key_quotes: So, perhaps, a quarter down the line, we will be able to give you better guidance in terms of how we are seeing those volumes coming up.
It's not a quarter-on-quarter business because of the fact that we operate in public health, so no quarter is going to be linear, whether sequentially or year on year.
So, we will hold this question probably to the next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Truenat franchise, the HPV validation, the two-year TB rate contract and the OptraScan FDA clearance. Cautious on near-term numbers: management repeatedly said quarters are non-linear, declined to size HPV volumes or give HPV timing until next quarter, and said OptraScan will not be profitable in FY27.

adds.what: Integrated R&D centre in Bangalore consolidating Bigtec staff (R&D, not production capacity)
Automation investment (~Rs 72 crore from IPO proceeds); no stated capacity addition

growth.why: Management guides FY27 top-line growth of roughly 25% and EBITDA margin of 24-25%, backed by a two-year TB rate contract signed last month, device volumes of 2,200-2,600 in line with history, and HPV rollout optionality; no new production capacity is planned, with kit utilisation at 58% and device at 42% providing headroom.
